errors.text: The initial state is incorrectly described as an already formed metastable FCC solid solution; the target starts from separate, nominally equimolar elemental powders.
The proposed VEC window of 7.5–8.0 is inconsistent with the approximate VEC of equiatomic CoCrFeNiTi, about 7.4, so the stated phase-stability criterion may exclude the composition being studied.
The mechanism conflates Ti-rich HCP precipitation with Laves-phase formation, although HCP and Laves phases are crystallographically and mechanistically distinct.

The cited evidence concerns Nb-doped CoCrFeNi, a Co-rich TRIP alloy, and AlCrFeNiV, and therefore does not directly establish the claimed Ti-specific HCP threshold or FCC-to-BCC transition in CoCrFeNiTi.
Low-load Vickers testing alone cannot isolate grain-boundary strengthening from precipitation hardening; matched grain-size and phase-fraction controls or annealing-based comparisons are required.
